t-hermit-island.st: A 1931 newspaper retelling says the recluse Wilson, who died in 1861, hid Mexican silver dollars; with Burnham (1929) that makes two tellings, but both are legend and no find has been confirmed.

t-hurley-saloons.st: Brody (1973, p 277) says lumberjacks and miners in the slab saloons were drunk, 'rolled' and thrown into Silver Street, and that 'the stockades' housed prostitutes. In the 1920s 'sin city' hosted booze runners and gunmen; one story tells of a man who shot dead someone asking what was in his suitcase.
src: Brody, Discovering Wisconsin (1973), p 277, borrowed copy
